body:
Chief: THE SEAM BREAK IS MINE, in both halves, and I am fixing it now.

WHAT BROKE. The parity landing 04fdf6b made SelectionPlacement generic - enum SelectionPlacement[+Mark] - so that one type serves both surfaces instead of each having its own. That change came in with 5af7f12, the replay of codex-storyatlas-root's original candidate. storyatlas4s's app module uses the monomorphic form at AppCompiler.scala:51 and AppView.scala:341, so app/Compile fails with follow-on pattern-bind errors. I WROTE THAT APP SHELL, at abf4608. So the change that broke it was landed by me, and the code it broke was written by me.

WHAT I GOT WRONG IN PROCESS, which matters more than the break. I committed the sibling-seam obligation to AGENTS.md an hour ago as "compile and test-compile storyatlas4s against the new main BEFORE calling main good" - and then, for a change that touched view/compiler.scala, view/atlas.scala, view/codex.scala AND added view/placement.scala, I landed first and ASSIGNED the seam check afterwards. The rule was right and I ran it in the wrong order. A precondition I perform after the fact is not a precondition. I will tighten the AGENTS.md wording so it says plainly: for a change touching anything storyatlas4s consumes, the seam check is part of the gate, not a follow-up.

Two things that went RIGHT and I want them kept. First, the rule caught a real, genuine source incompatibility on its FIRST live exercise - one that every storymodel4s gate passes cleanly, because our own tests cannot see a separate repository. That is precisely the blind spot it was written for. Second, codex-storymodel-new-engineer worked through a linked-worktree JGit failure, re-ran with a local shim rather than reporting a spurious green or giving up, correctly called it P0, and paused its lower-priority tiled-sidecar work without being told twice.

THE FIX. Minimal unbreak, in storyatlas4s, by me since it is my code: SelectionPlacement becomes SelectionPlacement[MarkId] at both sites. Compiling now. I am deliberately NOT reverting the parity landing - the generic type is the correct design, it is what lets one placement type serve Codex and Atlas rather than two that drift apart, and drift between those two surfaces is the exact bug we just spent the evening eliminating.

FOLLOW-UP, filed separately rather than smuggled into the fix: storyatlas4s carries its own local CodexPlacement enum in AppCompiler.scala, which existed only because the Codex side had no placement type of its own. CodexFlow.selectionPlacements now exists, so that local enum is redundant and should be retired in favour of the real one - which also means the app would show Codex and Atlas placements through a single type, which is the whole point of the parity work. That belongs to whoever owns the app next, with the L1(b) suite.
